selection_rationale: Major evidence-based transformation of German defence expenditure, officer leadership, NATO positioning, service law, permanent Lithuanian basing and whole-of-society logistics in 2026, explained through two world wars, post-1945 constitutional reconstruction and post-1990 demobilisation.
contrary_evidence: Fiscal budgets are authorised or proposed amounts, not receipts of materiel or deployable force; 2027 proposal should not be portrayed as 2027 actual spending.
Breuer's warning that Russia could possess capability to attack from 2029 explicitly does not mean Russia has decided to attack.
NATO Military Committee chair is a collective advisory office, not SACEUR or German command over Allied forces.
2026 military service remains primarily voluntary, with mandatory questionnaires for men and future medical assessment; compulsory enlistment requires further legal steps.
Historical German military aggression does not make contemporary parliamentary NATO defence identical to imperial or Nazi military institutions.
limitations: Budget categories of the national core budget, the Bundeswehr special fund and NATO expenditure ratios are not directly interchangeable.
End-2025 active personnel are observed, while 2026/2035 staffing and end-2027 Lithuanian brigade figures are planned targets.
OPLAN DEU full content remains classified: only public summary and quantified transit scenario can be analysed.
Assessment of Russian military capability from 2029 is a planning scenario, not independent verification of future attack intention.
Industrial throughput, availability of equipment, training and reserve deployability require rolling official confirmation.
Poll findings represent April–May 2026 respondents and vary by question and subgroup.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 3 November 2026, São Paulo local date. Primary-source military, legislative and parliamentary reports include September 2026 developments; no post-cutoff assertions.
producer_checks.research_depth: 18 analytical chapters per language; PT-BR 40,184 characters / 5,479 words; EN 39,394 characters / 5,058 words. Historical 1914–1945 through Weimar, Nazi wartime crimes, 1955 reconstitution, Cold War, 1990–2022 transformations, 2025–2026 fiscal shift, generals, deployment, manpower, industry, social support and 2027–2035 scenarios.
producer_checks.evidence_inventory: 25 numbered matching institutional and scholarly references per language, including Bundesarchiv, USHMM, DHM, Bundestag, Bundesbank, NATO, Bundeswehr and ZMSBw; factual qualifiers reflect source vintage.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Both languages contain two bar charts with the same arrays [[82.7,25.5,109.7,29.9],[184.2,186,190]], one two-chain causal flow, one five-region geopolitical map, one nine-row status/evidence table. Numeric labels and qualifications are consistent.
producer_checks.translation_check: Manual bilingual parity audit: identical 18 sections, 25 bibliography IDs, two chart value arrays, map regions and status tables; legal and temporal qualifications preserved.
producer_checks.factual_cautions: Distinguish 2027 budget proposal from 2026 appropriations and NATO-defined defence ratios; distinguish military service questionnaire and reserve planning from enacted mass conscription; do not equate committee advisory chair with NATO command authority.
producer_checks.editorial_status: Staged only. Public reports metadata must not be created without independent v2 QA approval. No conversational prose or public-facing meta editorial explanations.
producer_checks.source_cutoff: September 2026 military committee election, September 2026 Lithuanian brigade staffing document, September 2026 ZMSBw survey, Bundestag 2026/2027 budgets; historical records 1914–1955.

en.title: Germany's Military Awakening: From the First World War to Europe's Strategic Rearmament in 2026
en.deck: A historical and strategic investigation of German rearmament, from Hindenburg and the Wehrmacht to Breuer, Freuding, NATO's eastern flank, mobilisation, defence industry and parliamentary control.
en.regime: German defence has shifted from a limited expeditionary model to territorial and collective deterrence, while the scale of operating readiness lags behind fiscal and legal commitments.
en.key_risk: Confusing planned force levels and draft budget figures with fielded capability; equating constitutional German defence policy with historic aggressive militarism; presenting Breuer's 2029 capability warning as a confirmed Russian attack plan.
